title: Mpemba effect as an entropy-production race:Finite-amplitude bounds on crossing times in Markovian relaxation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two canonical preparations evolving under a common final Markov generator can exhibit the Mpemba effect because they excite different relaxation modes. We bound the first crossing of their relative entropies by treating relaxation as an entropy-production race. The exact balance $-\dot D=\dot e_p$ implies that a meeting occurs when the accumulated \emph{difference} of normalized entropy-production rates, $\int_0^t(r_H-r_C)\,\mathrm ds$ with $r_\alpha=\dot e_p^{\alpha}/D_\alpha$, equals the initial logarithmic deficit $\ln[D_H(0)/D_C(0)]$. Global entropy-decay inequalities yield a lower crossing-time bound when the entropy-decay constant is bounded from below and the hot rate from above; we supply both certificates. A nonzero cubic moment of a slowest eigenfunction is sufficient for the modified logarithmic Sobolev constant to lie strictly below the spectral gap. Combining established relative-entropy comparison inequalities with Markov contraction and the actual mode amplitudes gives finite-amplitude crossing bounds without a small-deviation expansion. For an exactly strong, reversible three-state preparation these give $0.1659\le t_M\le0.1674$ in model time units, independently certified by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. This interval is narrower than $1\%$ and contains $t_M=0.1662209$. The conservative global-rate comparison used here gives only $t_M\ge0.042$. The hotter preparation starts $6.12$ times farther from equilibrium, yet it reaches $D=10^{-5}$ at $t=0.233$, compared with $t=0.844$ for the colder one. Mean energy crosses later than relative entropy. For a fixed driven generator, nonadiabatic entropy production governs the same balance. These results concern finite-state relaxation in a specified distance and do not predict water-freezing times.
summary:
- Mpemba effect arises when two Markovian preparations excite different relaxation modes, modeled as an entropy‑production race.
- The first crossing of relative entropies occurs when the accumulated difference of normalized entropy‑production rates equals the initial logarithmic deficit, yielding lower bounds via entropy‑decay inequalities.
- Finite‑amplitude crossing bounds are derived without small‑deviation expansions; for a reversible three‑state system the crossing time is tightly bounded \(1659\le t_M\le1674\).

title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
authors: Sundeep Kapila, Bhaskaran Muralidharan, Satadeep Bhattacharjee
abstract: arXiv:2610.40729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbital contributions and guide systematic basis set refinement and optimizes parameters through weights. The resulting Hamiltonian can be used to evaluate anomalous (AHC) and spin Hall conductivities (SHC), and topological invariants. We demonstrate the framework using eight representative materials spanning semimetals, semiconductors, transition metals, f-electron compounds, and magnetic systems. Symmetry resolved models achieve band energy errors of 9 to 41 meV within 1 eV of the Fermi level. The fitted Hamiltonians reproduce characteristic features of the SHC response of Pt, the SOC dependence of the AHC of Fe, and the momentum dependent altermagnetic spin splitting of MnTe without any altermagnet specific interaction. For EuMn2Bi2, projection guided orbital refinement reduces the near Fermi level fitting error from 120 to 32 meV. Together, these results establish SKFitter as a flexible and reproducible framework for developing symmetry consistent, physically interpretable TB models of complex materials.

title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
authors: Rong Sun, Tolibjon Abdurakhmonov, Jan-Niklas Heidkamp, Julian Schr\"oer, Paul Weinbrenner, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tobias Korn, Oliver K\"uhn, Friedemann Reinhard
abstract: arXiv:2610.40733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.
summary:
- Co‑deposited terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hBN creates a ~1 nm alkane layer that disperses emitters without phase separation.
- Emitters can be tuned from ensembles to isolated single molecules, exhibiting blinking and suppressed diffusion confirmed by confocal, autocorrelation, and FRAP.
- Top‑side hBN encapsulation boosts photostability, yielding long‑lived emitters under high photon doses, enabling a 2D Shpolskii‑like matrix for quantum applications.

title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
authors: Y. Semerenko, N. Galtsov, D. Hurova, T. Bednarchuk, P. Zinoviev, V. Zoryansky, V. Moskalenko, R. Smolianets, A. Smirnov, Y. Pohribna, N. Aksenova
abstract: arXiv:2610.40737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work explores the structural relaxation of cryorolled commercially pure titanium subjected to subsequent annealing.Nanostructured specimens with an average grain size of ~50 nm were produced by plastic deformation via cryogenic rolling at 100 K to a true strain of 1.20, followed by annealing at 425 K, 525 K, 725 K, and 945 K. Microstructural evolution was examined using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. Cryogenic rolling was found to induce pronounced grain fragmentation, with coherent scattering regions (CSRs) of 30-50 nm dominating the substructure. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that annealing drives crystallite growth: a slight increase at 525 K, accelerated coarsening at 725 K, and complete recrystallization at 945 K. The kinetics of grain growth follow the classical Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner model, with a growth exponent of ~4, reflecting the role of triple junctions and defect-controlled boundary diffusion. The activation energy, estimated at ~97 kJ/mol, corresponds to typical values for grain boundary diffusion in {\alpha}-Ti, confirming that cryogenic deformation produces a highly non-equilibrium microstructure whose relaxation is strongly temperature dependent.
summary:
- Cryogenic rolling (100 K, true strain yields ~50 nm nanostructured Ti with 30–50 nm coherent scattering regions.
- Annealing (425–945 K) drives grain growth following LSW kinetics (exponent ≈ and full recrystallization at 945 K; activation energy ≈ 97 kJ mol⁻¹.
- Relaxation is highly temperature‑dependent, governed by defect‑controlled boundary diffusion and triple‑junction mechanisms.

title: Spectral properties of orthorhombic KSbOSiO$_4$ crystals: studies of infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiation absorption, Raman scattering, cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence
authors: Vladimir A. Yuryev, Tatyana V. Yuryeva, Ekaterina A. Morozova, Irina F. Kadikova, Polina A. Edelbekova
abstract: arXiv:2610.40739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystals of orthorhombic KSbOSiO$_4$ (KSS) are often found to synthesize in glass of historical and artistic articles. For instance, these crystallites in the glass of turquoise Bohemian seed beads are known to play a significant role in the process of internal-stress driven corrosion of the glass causing deterioration and destruction of bead embroidered museum exhibits, especially articles made in the early 19th century. In art materials science, KSS has been known since the mid-2010s only for its destructive effects on historical glass objects, but as an optical material it has long been studied. KSS belongs to the group of compounds isomorphic to KTiOPO$_4$ (KTP) and, like other compounds from this group, has anomalies in dielectric constant. The article presents the results of a study of orthorhombic KSS crystals using a number of spectroscopic techniques. IR absorption and diffuse reflection spectra of KSS in the spectral range from 50 to 4000~cm$^{-1}$, its Raman spectrum, its absorption spectrum in the range from near infrared to ultraviolet as well as its cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence spectra are investigated. The constituent peaks of the spectral bands are analyzed and their properties are summarized in tables; the allowed direct and indirect band gaps of KSS are determined. The presented data are necessary both for the correct spectral analysis of historical and artistic glass and enamels, during the production of which this substance was sometimes synthesized in glass, and for a more in-depth study of crystals of the KTP group.
summary:
- Comprehensive IR, Raman, UV‑Vis, cathodoluminescence, and photoluminescence spectra of orthorhombic KSbOSiO₄ (KSS) crystals, with peak assignments and band‑gap determination.
- Identification of direct and indirect band gaps and detailed spectral band constituents for KSS.
- Findings provide essential data for diagnosing KSS‑induced corrosion in historical glass and enamel artifacts.

title: Kibble-Zurek dynamics beyond the thermodynamic limit
authors: Max Haas, Guy C. Moore, Isaac M. Craig, Kristin A. Persson, Jiali He, Michael E. Hjelmstad, Dennis Meier, Sin\'ead M. Griffin, Jan Schulthei{\ss}
abstract: arXiv:2610.40755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predicts the universal scaling of topological defect densities generated during continuous phase transitions, a result derived in the thermodynamic limit of homogeneous systems. Yet real materials are intrinsically finite and heterogeneous, raising the question of how nonequilibrium universality survives outside this idealized limit. Here we establish an ensemble-finite-size extension of the KZM that describes critical dynamics in collections of independent finite subsystems with distributed sizes. We test this framework using a polycrystalline model system undergoing a symmetry-breaking transition. We find that the density of topological vortices follows an apparent power law with an exponent approximately half that observed in single crystals. This reduced exponent emerges quantitatively from averaging over the experimentally measured grain-size distribution, without fitting to the measured vortex densities. Our results demonstrate that finite-size effects do not simply suppress KZ scaling but reorganize it into an emergent statistical scaling regime governed by system-size heterogeneity. This establishes microstructure and geometry as control parameters of nonequilibrium critical dynamics and provides a general strategy to engineer scaling behaviour in complex materials.
summary:
- Extended Kibble‑Zurek mechanism to ensembles of finite, heterogeneous subsystems.
- In a polycrystalline model, vortex density scales with an exponent ≈ ½ of the single‑crystal value, explained by grain‑size averaging.
- Demonstrates microstructure geometry as a tunable control of nonequilibrium critical scaling.

title: Cavity-engineered ferroelectricity in SrTiO$_3$
authors: Omar Mehio, Sylvia Griffitt, Andrew Pierce, Emil V. Bostrom, Hanbyul Kim, Dylan P. Sotir, Darrell G. Schlom, Simone Latini, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, Dongbin Shin, Angel Rubio, Ankit S. Disa
abstract: arXiv:2610.40756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacing quantum materials with photonic cavity architectures is at the vanguard of materials engineering. The structured electromagnetic fluctuations of a dark cavity environment can renormalize fundamental thermodynamical material properties and energy scales, holding promise to create a rich ecosystem of cavity-induced ground states and functionalities absent in the bare material. However, direct experimental demonstrations that cavity coupling can stabilize or enhance genuinely new phases of matter have remained scarce. In this work, we establish the presence of cavity-induced and cavity-enhanced ferroelectric phases in free-standing SrTiO$_3$ membranes coupled to dark THz-frequency photonic crystal cavities. Using THz spectroscopy, we observe ultrastrong coupling (USC) between the ferroelectric soft mode in SrTiO$_3$ and the cavity resonance. The structural response of SrTiO$_3$ to this USC is measured via second harmonic generation imaging, which reveals a substantial (greater than 400%) enhancement of signal in the cavity environment and a distinct modification of the crystalline symmetry, indicating the onset and enhancement of ferroelectricity. We interpret these observations as resulting from renormalized piezoelectric and flexoelectric couplings, which in turn arise from the cavity-modified dielectric environment. This interpretation is supported with microscopic modeling via DFT-based multi-scale dynamics simulations and by macroscopic Ginzburg-Landau theory. Altogether, our experimental and theoretical results firmly confirm that cavity engineering can indeed be used to create new ground states in materials and enhance existing ones. This work establishes a new paradigm for materials engineering with direct applications for quantum transduction, quantum sensing, and nonlinear integrated photonics.
summary:
- Demonstrated cavity‑induced ferroelectricity in free‑standing SrTiO₃ membranes via ultrastrong coupling to THz photonic crystal cavities.
- THz spectroscopy and SHG imaging reveal >400 % signal enhancement and symmetry change, evidencing cavity‑enhanced ferroelectric soft mode.
- DFT‑based multi‑scale modeling attributes the effect to renormalized piezoelectric/flexoelectric couplings in the cavity‑modified dielectric environment.

title: Moir\'e metals and continuum models beyond a single valley
authors: Matthew Albert, Andrew Klekovkin-Hardy, Valentin Cr\'epel
abstract: arXiv:2610.40761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive continuum models of moir\'e materials valid over the full monolayer Brillouin zone, as required for metals whose large Fermi surfaces are not confined to a single valley. To this end, we introduce an environment-resolved two-center approximation, in which each hopping amplitude depends not only on the distance between the orbitals it connects but also on its position within the moir\'e cell. Taking the local environment to be set by the disregistry of the two layers alone, these moir\'e couplings and their full set of harmonics can be learnt from commensurate bilayers at uniform stackings, without fitting. The method shows excellent agreement with ab initio band structures on moir\'e cells containing a few hundred atoms. Applied to twisted NbSe$_2$, it yields a continuum model in which moir\'e effects concentrate at the van Hove singularities, a single-particle starting point for studying moir\'e-tuned superconducting, charge-density-wave instabilities and their competition.
summary:
- Developed a full‑BZ continuum model for moiré metals, extending beyond single‑valley approximations.
- Introduced an environment‑resolved two‑center hopping that depends on distance and moiré position, learned from commensurate bilayers without fitting.
- Applied to twisted NbSe₂, the model captures moiré‑induced van Hove singularities, providing a basis for studying superconductivity and CDW competition.

title: Gapless and Non-Equilibrium Topology in Blockaded Ladders
authors: Ramanjit Sohal, Hannes Bernien, Ruben Verresen
abstract: arXiv:2610.40771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a multi-leg PXYP model as a minimal setting to explore constraint-induced intertwinement between itinerant and internal degrees of freedom. We argue that the Rydberg-like blockade induces correlations in squeezed space, providing a unified mechanism for nontrivial string order both in and out of equilibrium. In a two-leg geometry, this leads to an intrinsically gapless topological ground state, which can terminate at a supersymmetric multicritical point. This mechanism also leads to the preservation of string order for parametrically long times after a quench, which we verify using tensor network simulations and a classical stochastic approximation to the dynamics. In a three-leg geometry, the blockade leads to an additional emergent $U(1)$ symmetry, resulting in a multicomponent Luttinger liquid where both itinerant and internal degrees of freedom are critical. This family of models arises naturally in a range of quantum simulator platforms such as Rydberg tweezer arrays and dipolar atoms in optical lattices.
summary:
- PXYP model with Rydberg‑like blockade creates squeezed‑space correlations, yielding nontrivial string order in and out of equilibrium.
- Two‑leg ladder hosts a gapless topological ground state that ends at a supersymmetric multicritical point; string order survives parametrically long after a quench.
- Three‑leg ladder develops an emergent U(symmetry, forming a multicomponent Luttinger liquid where itinerant and internal degrees of freedom are simultaneously critical.

title: Singlet-Triplet Transition of Rotating Moir\'e Atoms in a Magnetic Field
authors: Conor Smith, Yubo Yang, Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales
abstract: arXiv:2610.40786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices can bind several electrons to each potential minimum, forming few-electron "moir\'e atoms." Using neural quantum states that obey magnetic periodic boundary conditions, include full Landau-level mixing, and treat both spin sectors, we map the ground state of two-electron moir\'e atoms in a superlattice as a function of moir\'e depth and magnetic field strength. At strong field each atom is a spin-triplet maximum-density droplet with canonical angular momentum $\langle L_z\rangle=-1$ and a persistent circulating current: the rotating counterpart of the "Wigner molecular crystal" recently imaged in moir\'e superlattices. Deepening the wells drives a singlet-triplet transition to non-rotating spin-singlet atoms whose only current is a weak diamagnetic counter-circulation. The transition moves to deeper wells as the field grows, so depth and field together open a window for the formation of rotors. This is the collective analog of the singlet-triplet transition of two-electron quantum dots. At the transition, the orbital magnetic moments of the atoms reverse sign as their spin polarization switches, a joint signature accessible to magnetometry. If the atoms are instead polarized by other means, such as magnetic proximity coupling, the rotors lock at weak field into a spontaneously ordered crystal of dimers in a pinwheel pattern.
summary:
- Two‑electron moiré atoms switch from spin‑triplet rotating droplets (Lz = –to spin‑singlet non‑rotating states as well depth increases.
- The singlet‑triplet transition moves to deeper wells with stronger magnetic field, opening a window for rotating “rotors” whose orbital moments reverse sign at the transition.
- Proximity‑induced spin polarization locks rotors into a pinwheel dimer crystal at weak field, providing a magnetometry signature.

title: Quantum Monte-Carlo study of spin-valley ferromagnetism in rhombohedral graphene
authors: Michael Demos, Dongqi Li, Mainak Das, Tobias M. R. Wolf, Chunli Huang
abstract: arXiv:2610.40864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at $T_c \approx 0.7$ K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.

title: Triplon thermal Hall response in a honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions
authors: Guilherme F. Figueiredo, E. Miranda, R. L. Doretto
abstract: arXiv:2610.40910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate triplon topology and the thermal Hall transport in a columnar valence-bond solid of a spin-$1/2$ honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Inequivalent triangular sublattices, modeled by $J_2^A\neq J_2^B$, remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and allow in-plane Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions. We identify the two symmetry-allowed in-plane DM vector patterns and present detailed results for the pattern parallel to the bonds including an out-of-plane magnetic field. Within a harmonic bond-operator treatment, we determine the triplon bands, their Berry curvatures and Chern numbers, and the triplon thermal Hall conductivity. The DM interaction and magnetic field generate nonzero Berry curvatures, but the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated triplon band vanishes. Nevertheless, the energy-dependent Bose weighting of positive and negative Berry-curvature regions produces a finite thermal Hall response at nonzero low temperatures. We delimit the dilute-triplon regime in which the harmonic transport calculation is expected to be reliable. These results show that a vanishing Chern number band does not directly constrain the triplon response of a valence-bond solid. We also comment on the effects on the columnar valence-bond solid phase of a DM interaction between next-nearest-neighbor spins characterized by an out-of-plane vector pattern.
summary:
- Honeycomb‑lattice \(J_1\!-\!J_2\) VBS with \(J_2^A\neq J_2^B\) breaks inversion, enabling in‑plane DM vectors.
- Harmonic bond‑operator treatment shows DM + field generate Berry curvature (zero Chern number per band) yet yield finite low‑\(T\) triplon thermal Hall conductivity.
- Dilute‑triplon regime is identified; vanishing Chern numbers do not forbid thermal Hall response, and next‑nearest‑neighbor DM effects are discussed.

title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by overdamped vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
authors: Leonardo Celada, Rocco Bellusci, D. K. Andrea Phan-Huu, Alessandro Chiesa, Stefano Carretta
abstract: arXiv:2610.40990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), we investigate spin polarization during molecular electron transfer through a correlated bridge in the presence of a rapidly relaxing Peierls mode. By modulating both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling, the mode mediates two-body spin-spin interactions, including isotropic, anisotropic, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange. We derive these interactions using an exact Lang-Firsov transformation for a four-site chiral bridge. We then include fast vibrational relaxation in the joint electron--vibration master equation and derive the reduced electronic dynamics to second order in the vibronic coupling, retaining both coherent and dissipative contributions and the finite-time buildup of the vibrational response. We test our derivation by numerical simulations, finding spin polarization accumulated at the acceptor after unpolarized injection, with nonmonotonic dependence on damping and bridge filling. Within the postulated local-loss model, our results show that rapid vibrational relaxation does not preclude spin polarization through a correlated bridge and provide a framework for assessing vibration-mediated interactions and dissipative dynamics as ingredients of CISS in molecular electron transfer.
summary:
- Derived Peierls‑mode–mediated two‑body spin interactions (isotropic, anisotropic, Dzyaloshinskii‑Moriya) on a four‑site chiral bridge via Lang‑Firsov transformation.
- Formulated a master‑equation including fast vibrational relaxation, capturing coherent and dissipative spin dynamics to second order in vibronic coupling.
- Numerical simulations show acceptor spin polarization from unpolarized injection, with nonmonotonic dependence on damping and bridge filling, confirming CISS viability under rapid vibrational relaxation.

title: Multiband-Induced Complex Magnetotransport in the Kagome Metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$
authors: Hongye Zhang, Xingyu Ma, Ying Zhu, Jingyang Zhu, Andreas Eich, Yuan Tang, Xiong Wang, Ningxi Yang, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xinrun Mi, Michael Merz, Quansheng Wu, Mingquan He
abstract: arXiv:2610.41409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the electrical transport properties of the kagome metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$, which undergoes a charge density wave (CDW) transition at $T_\mathrm{CDW}\approx80$ K. Similar to the kagome metals $A$V$_3$Sb$_5$ ($A$ = K, Rb, Cs), LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$ develops complex magnetotransport behavior near and below the CDW transition. In particular, the longitudinal magnetoconductivity exhibits an approximately linear field dependence below about 1 T, whereas the field dependence of Hall conductivity displays pronounced nonlinearity and a field-induced sign reversal. Although an anomalous Hall-like contribution can be extracted by subtracting a local background from the Hall conductivity, mobility-spectrum analysis shows that the overall magnetotransport can be largely accounted for by multiband conduction involving high-mobility electronlike and holelike carriers. Nevertheless, sizable deviations from the multiband model emerge near $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, pointing to additional CDW-related scattering processes. These results demonstrate that high-mobility multiband transport, together with CDW-induced modifications of carrier scattering, play important roles in the complex magnetotransport of LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$.
summary:
- LuNb₆Sn₆ undergoes a CDW transition at ~80 K, below which its magnetotransport becomes highly non‑linear.
- Longitudinal conductivity is linear in field below ~1 T, while Hall conductivity shows strong nonlinearity and a field‑induced sign reversal, consistent with high‑mobility multiband electron and hole carriers.
- Near T_CDW, deviations from the multiband model reveal additional CDW‑related scattering affecting carrier dynamics.

title: Counting kinks and magnons with the lattice: magnetoelastic effects in Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$
authors: V. Romerio, J. Nagl, K. Yu. Povarov, S. Gvasaliya, A. Zheludev
abstract: arXiv:2610.41619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the N\'eel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.
summary:
- Dilatometry and ultrasound reveal all field‑induced magnetic phases in Cs₂CoBr₄, with distinct lattice anomalies at each transition.
- Chain‑axis elongation tracks magnetization, interpreted as kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in transverse‑ordered BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion.
- Joint ultrasound‑striction analysis quantifies the magnetoelastic coupling strength throughout the phase diagram.
